ml.ApproxCountDistinctFunction.description: Computes the approximate count of distinct values.

input.description: The input column from which the approximate count of distinct values is computed.

relative_error.description:
The error the user accepts, as a fraction of the count, between 0.02 (by default) and 0.3.
This is one standard error of the estimate, the same meaning as Spark's relativeSD: 0.02 means
the result is within ±2% of the true count about 68% of the time (one standard deviation covers
68% of the region). Feature Store picks the sketch size that gives this relative error. If
neither relative_error nor relative_sd is set, 0.02 is default chosen at feature creation.

relative_sd.description:
The maximum relative standard deviation allowed (default defined by Spark).
Deprecated: use relative_error. When relative_error is set, reads return the same value here
for clients that don't have relative_error, and a request may only send that value.

ml.ApproxPercentileFunction.description: Computes the approximate percentile of values.

accuracy.description:
The accuracy parameter (higher is more accurate but slower).
Deprecated: use relative_error. When relative_error is set, reads return ceil(1 /
relative_error) here for clients that don't have relative_error, and a request may only send
that value.

input.description: The input column from which the approximate percentile is computed.

percentile.description: The percentile value to compute (between 0 and 1).

relative_error.description:
The error the user accepts, as a fraction of rank, between 0.01 (by default) and 0.3. The
result is within this rank error with 99% confidence: at 0.01, the value returned for p95 is
between the true p94 and p96 at least 99% of the time. Feature Store picks the sketch size that
gives this error.
If neither relative_error nor accuracy is set, 0.01 is default chosen at feature creation.

ml.CreateRegistryWebhook.description: Details required to create a registry webhook.

events.description:
Events that can trigger a registry webhook:
* `MODEL_VERSION_CREATED`: A new model version was created for the associated model.

* `MODEL_VERSION_TRANSITIONED_STAGE`: A model version’s stage was changed.

* `TRANSITION_REQUEST_CREATED`: A user requested a model version’s stage be transitioned.

* `COMMENT_CREATED`: A user wrote a comment on a registered model.

* `REGISTERED_MODEL_CREATED`: A new registered model was created. This event type can only be specified for a registry-wide webhook, which can be created by not specifying a model name in the create request.

* `MODEL_VERSION_TAG_SET`: A user set a tag on the model version.

* `MODEL_VERSION_TRANSITIONED_TO_STAGING`: A model version was transitioned to staging.

* `MODEL_VERSION_TRANSITIONED_TO_PRODUCTION`: A model version was transitioned to production.

* `MODEL_VERSION_TRANSITIONED_TO_ARCHIVED`: A model version was archived.

* `TRANSITION_REQUEST_TO_STAGING_CREATED`: A user requested a model version be transitioned to staging.

* `TRANSITION_REQUEST_TO_PRODUCTION_CREATED`: A user requested a model version be transitioned to production.

* `TRANSITION_REQUEST_TO_ARCHIVED_CREATED`: A user requested a model version be archived.

http_url_spec.description: External HTTPS URL called on event trigger (by using a POST request).

job_spec.description: ID of the job that the webhook runs.

model_name.description: If model name is not specified, a registry-wide webhook is created that listens for the specified events across all versions of all registered models.

status.description:
Enable or disable triggering the webhook, or put the webhook into test mode. The default is `ACTIVE`:
* `ACTIVE`: Webhook is triggered when an associated event happens.

* `DISABLED`: Webhook is not triggered.

* `TEST_MODE`: Webhook can be triggered through the test endpoint, but is not triggered on a real event.

schedule is interpreted in timezone_id (defaults to UTC). Required when mode is MANUAL (or

A Java timezone ID. The schedule is resolved with respect to this timezone. Defaults to UTC
when omitted. Can only be configured for MANUAL schedules; DERIVED schedules are always aligned
to UTC.

Events that trigger the webhook.
* `MODEL_VERSION_CREATED`: A new model version was created for the associated model.

* `MODEL_VERSION_TRANSITIONED_STAGE`: A model version’s stage was changed.

* `MODEL_VERSION_TRANSITIONED_TO_STAGING`: A model version was transitioned to staging.

* `MODEL_VERSION_TRANSITIONED_TO_PRODUCTION`: A model version was transitioned to production.

* `MODEL_VERSION_TRANSITIONED_TO_ARCHIVED`: A model version was archived.

* `TRANSITION_REQUEST_TO_PRODUCTION_CREATED`: A user requested a model version be transitioned to production.

* `TRANSITION_REQUEST_TO_ARCHIVED_CREATED`: A user requested a model version be archived.

If `events` is specified, any webhook with one or more of the specified trigger events is included in the output.
If `events` is not specified, webhooks of all event types are included in the output.

every failed attempt, including attempts that will be retried.

Batch materialization does not retry failures that need a fix on your side, such as missing
permissions or invalid configuration, so the first attempt is the final one. Other batch
failures are retried up to twice.

retried. With this set, a streaming materialized feature notifies only on errors that cannot
be retried, and never on failures that are restarted.

Gap in sequence number is intentional and is done in order to
match field sequence numbers of `ModelVersion` proto message

run_id.description: Unique identifier for the MLflow tracking run associated with the source model artifacts.

run_link.description: URL of the run associated with the model artifacts. This field is set at model version creation time only for model versions whose source run is from a tracking server that is different from the registry server.

source.description: URI that indicates the location of the source model artifacts. This is used when creating the model version.

status_message.description: Details on the current status, for example why registration failed.

tags.description: Array of tags that are associated with the model version.

user_id.description: The username of the user that created the object.

ml.ModelVersionStatus.description:
The status of the model version. Valid values are:
* `PENDING_REGISTRATION`: Request to register a new model version is pending as server performs background tasks.

* `FAILED_REGISTRATION`: Request to register a new model version has failed.

* `READY`: Model version is ready for use.

enum_descriptions.FAILED_REGISTRATION: Request to register a new model version has failed.
enum_descriptions.PENDING_REGISTRATION: Request to register a new model version is pending as server performs background tasks.
enum_descriptions.READY: Model version is ready for use.

ml.MtlsConfig.description:
Mutual-TLS (mTLS) authentication configuration. The keystore (client certificate +
private key) and truststore (CAs trusted to verify the broker) live as JKS files on
Unity Catalog volumes, with their passwords stored in Databricks secret scopes. This
matches the SSL setup pattern documented at
https://docs.databricks.com/en/connect/streaming/kafka/authentication#use-ssl-to-connect-databricks-to-kafka.

disable_hostname_verification.description:
Set to true only when the broker certificate's SAN intentionally does not match
the connection endpoint — for example when reaching the cluster through a
PrivateLink endpoint whose DNS name is not in the broker certificate. Skipping
the hostname check removes a defense against man-in-the-middle attacks; do not
enable casually. mTLS client authentication is unaffected by this option.

See the Apache Kafka SSL security guide for background on this check:
https://kafka.apache.org/42/security/encryption-and-authentication-using-ssl/#host-name-verification

key_password_ref.description:
Secret-scope reference for the private key password. Often the same value as the
keystore password (keytool's default), but provided as a separate field because
Apache Kafka requires it as a distinct option (kafka.ssl.key.password).

keystore_location.description:
Unity Catalog volume path to the JKS keystore file containing the client certificate
and private key. e.g. "/Volumes/<catalog>/<schema>/<volume>/client.jks". The
materialization compute must have read permission on this volume.

keystore_password_ref.description: Secret-scope reference for the JKS keystore password.

truststore_location.description:
Unity Catalog volume path to the JKS truststore file containing the CA certificate(s)
trusted to verify the Kafka broker's server certificate.
e.g. "/Volumes/<catalog>/<schema>/<volume>/truststore.jks".

truststore_password_ref.description: Secret-scope reference for the JKS truststore password.

table_name_prefix.description:
Prefix for Unity Catalog table name.
The materialized feature will be stored in a table with this prefix and a generated postfix.

ml.OnlineStore.description: An OnlineStore is a logical database instance that stores and serves features online.

capacity.description: The capacity of the online store. Valid values are "CU_1", "CU_2", "CU_4", "CU_8".

creation_time.description: The timestamp when the online store was created.

creator.description: The email of the creator of the online store.

name.description: The name of the online store. This is the unique identifier for the online store.

read_replica_count.description: The number of read replicas for the online store. Defaults to 0.

state.description: The current state of the online store.

usage_policy_id.description: The usage policy applied to the online store to track billing.

catalog_name.description:
The Unity Catalog catalog name. This name is also used as the Lakebase logical database name.
Quoting is handled by the backend where needed, do not pre-quote it.

online_store_name.description: The name of the target online store.

schema_name.description:
The Unity Catalog schema name. This name is also used as the Lakebase schema name under the database.
Quoting is handled by the backend where needed, do not pre-quote it.

table_name_prefix.description:
Prefix for Unity Catalog table name.
The materialized feature will be stored in a Lakebase table with this prefix and a generated postfix.

ml.Operation.description:
This resource represents a long-running operation that is the result of a
network API call.

done.description:
If the value is `false`, it means the operation is still in progress.
If `true`, the operation is completed, and either `error` or `response` is
available.

error.description: The error result of the operation in case of failure or cancellation.

metadata.description:
Service-specific metadata associated with the operation.  It typically
contains progress information and common metadata such as create time.
Some services might not provide such metadata.

name.description:
The server-assigned name, which is only unique within the same service that
originally returns it. If you use the default HTTP mapping, the
`name` should be a resource name ending with `operations/{unique_id}`.

response.description: The normal, successful response of the operation.

ml.PermissionLevel.description:
Permission level of the requesting user on the object. For what is allowed at each level, see
[MLflow Model permissions](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/machine-learning/manage-model-lifecycle/workspace-model-registry#permissions).

ml.ProtoSchemaSpec.description:
A Protocol Buffer schema paired with the name of the message within it that describes the
Kafka payload. A .proto file may declare multiple messages; message_name disambiguates.

message_name.description:
The fully-qualified name of the message within schema_text that describes the Kafka payload
(e.g. "Event" or "com.example.Event" if schema_text declares a package). Identifies which
message is used to decode each Kafka record — a .proto file may declare multiple messages
but only one represents the payload. Must not be empty.

schema_text.description:
The raw .proto file text (proto2 and proto3 syntax supported, see
https://protobuf.dev/programming-guides/proto3/ and https://protobuf.dev/programming-guides/proto2/).

budget_policy_id.description:
Budget policy id used to attribute the serverless compute cost of the synced online-table sync
pipeline. Applied only when the sync pipeline is first created (the initial publish of a new
online table); republishing to an existing online table does not update it.

full_feature_name.description:
Full Unity Catalog name of one of the features materialized in the source table, used to
derive the synced online table's entity and timeseries columns. Required for view sources
without a UC PrimaryKeyConstraint; ignored when the source already has one.

online_store.description: The name of the target online store.

online_table_name.description: The full three-part (catalog, schema, table) name of the online table.

publish_mode.description: The publish mode of the pipeline that syncs the online table with the source table.

tags.description:
Custom tags to apply to the synced online-table sync pipeline created for this publish. They
are forwarded to the pipeline's compute as cluster tags so its cost can be attributed in the
billing system tables. Applied only when the sync pipeline is first created (the initial
publish of a new online table); republishing to an existing online table does not update them.

publish_spec.description: The specification for publishing the online table from the source table.

online_table_name.description: The full three-part (catalog, schema, table) name of the online table.

pipeline_id.description: The ID of the pipeline that syncs the online table with the source table.

ml.PurgeFeatureEntitiesMetadata.description: Progress and configuration for a feature entity purge.

create_time.description: Time at which the purge operation was created.

delete_rows.description: Whether this purge deletes matching rows instead of setting feature values to null.

entities_table.description: Fully qualified name of the Unity Catalog Delta table containing the entity keys to purge.

entities_table_version.description: Version of the entities table used by the purge.

features.description: Fully qualified names of the features targeted by the purge.

job_id.description: ID of the job that executes this purge.

state.description: Current state of the purge operation.

ml.PurgeFeatureEntitiesMetadataState.description: Lifecycle state of a feature entity purge.

ml.PurgeFeatureEntitiesRequest.description: Request to purge materialized feature values for entities listed in a Unity Catalog Delta table.

budget_policy_id.description:
The budget policy ID, in UUID format, used to attribute the serverless compute cost of this
purge. If not specified, a default budget policy may be applied.

delete_rows.description:
If false feature values are set to null on purge but rows are not deleted. If true then the full rows containing entities are deleted. Defaults to false.
When true, the request must include every feature which shares the same `table_name` property in their MaterializedFeature.
Features from multiple tables may be included if all features materialized in each table are included.

entities_table.description:
Fully qualified name of the Unity Catalog Delta table containing the entity keys to purge.
The table may contain a subset of each feature's entity-key columns. A partial key match
deletes all feature rows matching the provided key values. Non-key columns are rejected;
null key values are allowed.

features.description:
Fully qualified names of the features to purge. At least one nonempty feature name is required.
A request may contain at most 500 features; submit additional features in separate requests.
Duplicate features are rejected.

request_id.description: Optional UUID4 idempotency token for the request.

tags.description:
Custom tags to associate with this purge. They are applied to the purge job and forwarded to
the underlying compute as Databricks resource tags, so purge cost can be attributed in the
billing system tables. These tags apply only to the purge compute; they are not applied to the
Unity Catalog Feature resources themselves, whose tags are managed separately through the Unity
Catalog tagging API. A maximum of 25 tags is supported; keys and values are subject to the same
limitations as Databricks resource tags.

ml.PurgeFeatureEntitiesResponse.description: Result of a completed feature entity purge.

error.description: Operation-level error, if the purge failed outside an individual feature target.
Error encountered while purging this feature, if any.

feature.description: Fully qualified name of the feature that was purged.

offline_state.description: State of the offline purge for this feature.

online_state.description: State of the online purge for this feature.

ml.PurgeFeatureEntitiesResultState.description: Terminal state of a purge for one store type.

service_principal_name.description: application ID of a service principal

display_name.description: Display name of the user or service principal.

ml.RegistryEmailSubscriptionType.description:
.. note::
Experimental: This entity may change or be removed in a future release without warning.
Email subscription types for registry notifications:
- `ALL_EVENTS`: Subscribed to all events.
- `DEFAULT`: Default subscription type.
- `SUBSCRIBED`: Subscribed to notifications.
- `UNSUBSCRIBED`: Not subscribed to notifications.

creation_timestamp.description: Creation time of the object, as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

events.description:
Events that can trigger a registry webhook:
* `MODEL_VERSION_CREATED`: A new model version was created for the associated model.

* `MODEL_VERSION_TRANSITIONED_STAGE`: A model version’s stage was changed.

* `TRANSITION_REQUEST_CREATED`: A user requested a model version’s stage be transitioned.

* `COMMENT_CREATED`: A user wrote a comment on a registered model.

* `REGISTERED_MODEL_CREATED`: A new registered model was created. This event type can only be specified for a registry-wide webhook, which can be created by not specifying a model name in the create request.

* `MODEL_VERSION_TAG_SET`: A user set a tag on the model version.

* `MODEL_VERSION_TRANSITIONED_TO_STAGING`: A model version was transitioned to staging.

* `MODEL_VERSION_TRANSITIONED_TO_PRODUCTION`: A model version was transitioned to production.

* `MODEL_VERSION_TRANSITIONED_TO_ARCHIVED`: A model version was archived.

* `TRANSITION_REQUEST_TO_STAGING_CREATED`: A user requested a model version be transitioned to staging.

* `TRANSITION_REQUEST_TO_PRODUCTION_CREATED`: A user requested a model version be transitioned to production.

* `TRANSITION_REQUEST_TO_ARCHIVED_CREATED`: A user requested a model version be archived.

last_updated_timestamp.description: Time of the object at last update, as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

model_name.description: Name of the model whose events would trigger this webhook.

ml.RegistryWebhookStatus.description:
Enable or disable triggering the webhook, or put the webhook into test mode. The default is `ACTIVE`:
* `ACTIVE`: Webhook is triggered when an associated event happens.

* `DISABLED`: Webhook is not triggered.

* `TEST_MODE`: Webhook can be triggered through the test endpoint, but is not triggered on a real event.

enum_descriptions.ACTIVE: Webhook is triggered when an associated event happens.
enum_descriptions.TEST_MODE: Webhook can be triggered through the test endpoint, but is not triggered on a real event.

ml.RejectTransitionRequest.description: Details required to identify and reject a model version stage transition request.

stage.description:
Target stage of the transition. Valid values are:

* `None`: The initial stage of a model version.

* `Staging`: Staging or pre-production stage.

* `Production`: Production stage.

* `Archived`: Archived stage.

activity.description: New activity generated as a result of this operation.

new_name.description: If provided, updates the name for this `registered_model`.

ml.RequestSource.description: A request-time data source whose value is provided at inference time: offline batch scoring or online serving endpoint

dataframe_schema.description:
A schema containing scalar or nested fields, in Spark StructType JSON format
(from df.schema.json()). This preserves field, array-element, and map-value nullability.

flat_schema.description: A flat schema with scalar-typed fields only.

run_id.description: ID of the run to restore.

experiment_id.description: The ID of the experiment containing the runs to restore.

max_runs.description:
An optional positive integer indicating the maximum number of runs to restore. The maximum allowed value for
max_runs is 10000.

min_timestamp_millis.description:
The minimum deletion timestamp in milliseconds since the UNIX epoch for restoring runs. Only runs deleted no
earlier than this timestamp are restored.

ml.RollingWindow.description: A rolling time window with an optional non-negative delay.

delay.description:
Non-negative analytic lag that evaluates the window this far in the past. Use this for timing
variations unrelated to source lateness, such as a 30-day count as of one week ago. If unset,
the analytic lag is zero. It composes with source.lateness when both are set.

window_duration.description:
The duration of the rolling window. Must be positive when set; absent means lifetime
(aggregate over the entity's entire history).

tags.description: Additional metadata key-value pairs.

artifact_uri.description:
URI of the directory where artifacts should be uploaded.
This can be a local path (starting with "/"), or a distributed file system (DFS)
path, like ``s3://bucket/directory`` or ``dbfs:/my/directory``.
If not set, the local ``./mlruns`` directory is  chosen.

end_time.description: Unix timestamp of when the run ended in milliseconds.

lifecycle_stage.description: Current life cycle stage of the experiment : OneOf("active", "deleted")

run_uuid.description:
[Deprecated, use run_id instead] Unique identifier for the run. This field will
be removed in a future MLflow version.

start_time.description: Unix timestamp of when the run started in milliseconds.

user_id.description:
User who initiated the run.
This field is deprecated as of MLflow 1.0, and will be removed in a future
MLflow release. Use 'mlflow.user' tag instead.

ml.SawtoothWindow.description:
A sawtooth window served via the hybrid batch + streaming path. The batch pipeline maintains
daily partial aggregates for the bulk of the window while the streaming pipeline maintains the
most recent day(s), and serving merges them on read. Same field shape as RollingWindow, but a
distinct type so the control plane can explicitly identify hybrid (sawtooth) features rather
than inferring hybrid behavior from window_duration.

delay.description: Delay is not currently supported for Sawtooth windows.

window_duration.description:
The duration of the window. Must be positive and span more than two days when set, so that both
the batch (N-1 day) and stale-path (N-2 day) partial aggregates are well defined. The duration
need not be a whole number of days (e.g. 3 days 15 minutes is allowed). Absent means lifetime
(aggregate over the entity's entire history).

ml.ScalarDataType.description:
Scalar data types for request-time field definitions.
Only flat (non-nested) types are supported.

json_schema.description: Schema of the JSON object in standard IETF JSON schema format (https://json-schema.org/).

proto_schema.description: Protocol Buffer schema with its payload message name.

ml.SchemaLocator.description:
Schema locator for one side (payload or key) of a message.
Identifies which schema to use in the schema registry and the serialization format.

ml.SchemaLocatorConfluentSchema.description:
Confluent Schema Registry schema locator.
The value to provide for `subject` depends on the naming strategy configured in your registry:
- TopicNameStrategy (default): "{topic}-key" or "{topic}-value"
e.g. for topic "transactions" use "transactions-value" for the payload and "transactions-key" for the key.
- RecordNameStrategy: the fully-qualified record name
e.g. "com.example.Payment" for Avro, the bare message name (without package) for Protobuf,
or the `title` field value for JSON.
- TopicRecordNameStrategy: "{topic}-{fully-qualified-record-name}"
e.g. "transactions-com.example.Payment".

subject.description: The Confluent schema registry subject name.

ml.SchemaLocatorFormat.description: Supported serialization formats for a schema registry schema.

ml.SchemaRegistryConfig.description: Configuration for resolving a Stream's schema from an external schema registry (e.g. Confluent).

api_secret_ref.description:
Reference to the schema registry API secret in a Databricks secret scope.
Set this only if required for authentication for the schema registry.

key_schema_locator.description:
Schema locator for the message key. Only used for Kafka streams.
At least one of payload_schema_locator or key_schema_locator must be set.

payload_schema_locator.description:
Schema locator for the message payload. For Kafka this is the value.
At least one of payload_schema_locator or key_schema_locator must be set.

uc_connection.description: A Schema Registry UC Connection object.

ml.SdpSource.description: A Spark Declarative Pipeline (SDP) data source.

filter_condition.description: Single WHERE clause to filter the pipeline's output table before applying transformations. Will be row-wise evaluated, so should only include conditionals and projections.

input_tables.description:
The full three-part names of the tables the pipeline reads from. Required to materialize this
feature with a TableTrigger, which starts a run when these tables update. Each table must exist
when the feature is created. Feature Store doesn't confirm that the pipeline reads from these
tables. At most 100 tables.

output_table.description:
The full three-part (catalog, schema, table) name of the pipeline's output table to read from.
The table doesn't need to exist until the pipeline first runs. Required.

pipeline_id.description:
The ID of the Spark Declarative Pipeline that Feature Store runs to produce this source, before
each materialization or backfill. The pipeline must already exist when the feature is created,
and you need CAN_RUN, CAN_MANAGE, or owner permission on it. It doesn't need to have run yet.
Deleting the feature doesn't delete the pipeline. If the pipeline is deleted, this field reads
back empty. Required.

pipeline_state.description:
State tracking pipeline execution and output table validation. PENDING until the pipeline
has run at least once and created the output table; then RESOLVED on success, or ERROR on failure.

transformation_sql.description:
A single SQL SELECT expression applied after filter_condition.
Should contain all the columns needed (eg. "SELECT *, col_a + col_b AS col_c FROM x.y.z WHERE col_a > 0" would have `transformation_sql` "*, col_a + col_b AS col_c")
If transformation_sql is not provided, all columns of the pipeline's output table are present in the DataSource dataframe.

ml.SdpSourceState.description: State of the SDP source relative to pipeline execution and output table validation.

filter.description: String representing a SQL filter condition (e.g. "name ILIKE 'my-experiment%'")

max_results.description: Maximum number of experiments desired. Max threshold is 3000.

order_by.description:
List of columns for ordering search results, which can include experiment name and last updated
timestamp with an optional "DESC" or "ASC" annotation, where "ASC" is the default.
Tiebreaks are done by experiment id DESC.

page_token.description: Token indicating the page of experiments to fetch

view_type.description:
Qualifier for type of experiments to be returned.
If unspecified, return only active experiments.

experiments.description: Experiments that match the search criteria

next_page_token.description:
Token that can be used to retrieve the next page of experiments.
An empty token means that no more experiments are available for retrieval.

categories.description: Matches Issues with any of these categories, case-insensitively.

page_size.description: Defaults to 20; values above 100 are clamped.

page_token.description:
Expires after 15 minutes. Every other argument except `view` must match the
request that returned the token.

severities.description: Matches Issues with any of these severities.

statuses.description:
Matches Issues with any of these statuses. Different filters AND together,
and an empty filter matches every Issue.

tag_filters.description:
Matches Issues that satisfy every filter. At most 10 filters of 20 values
each.

issues.description: The page's Issues, in the requested order.

ascending.description: Whether the search results order is ascending or not.

dataset_digest.description:
If ``field_name`` refers to a metric, this field specifies the digest of the dataset
associated with the metric. Only metrics associated with the specified dataset name
and digest will be considered for ordering. This field may only be set if ``dataset_name``
is also set.

dataset_name.description:
If ``field_name`` refers to a metric, this field specifies the name of the dataset
associated with the metric. Only metrics associated with the specified dataset name will be
considered for ordering. This field may only be set if ``field_name`` refers to a metric.

field_name.description: The name of the field to order by, e.g. "metrics.accuracy".

datasets.description:
List of datasets on which to apply the metrics filter clauses.
For example, a filter with `metrics.accuracy > 0.9` and dataset info with name "test_dataset"
means we will return all logged models with accuracy > 0.9 on the test_dataset.
Metric values from ANY dataset matching the criteria are considered.
If no datasets are specified, then metrics across all datasets are considered in the filter.

experiment_ids.description: The IDs of the experiments in which to search for logged models.

filter.description:
A filter expression over logged model info and data that allows returning a subset of
logged models. The syntax is a subset of SQL that supports AND'ing together binary operations.

Example: ``params.alpha < 0.3 AND metrics.accuracy > 0.9``.

max_results.description: The maximum number of Logged Models to return. The maximum limit is 50.

order_by.description: The list of columns for ordering the results, with additional fields for sorting criteria.

page_token.description: The token indicating the page of logged models to fetch.

models.description: Logged models that match the search criteria.

next_page_token.description: The token that can be used to retrieve the next page of logged models.

filter.description:
String filter condition, like "name='my-model-name'". Must be a single boolean condition,
with string values wrapped in single quotes.

max_results.description: Maximum number of models desired. Max threshold is 10K.

order_by.description:
List of columns to be ordered by including model name, version, stage with an
optional "DESC" or "ASC" annotation, where "ASC" is the default.
Tiebreaks are done by latest stage transition timestamp, followed by name ASC, followed by
version DESC.

page_token.description: Pagination token to go to next page based on previous search query.

model_versions.description: Models that match the search criteria

next_page_token.description: Pagination token to request next page of models for the same search query.

filter.description:
String filter condition, like "name LIKE 'my-model-name'".
Interpreted in the backend automatically as "name LIKE '%my-model-name%'".
Single boolean condition, with string values wrapped in single quotes.

max_results.description: Maximum number of models desired. Default is 100. Max threshold is 1000.

order_by.description:
List of columns for ordering search results, which can include model name and last updated
timestamp with an optional "DESC" or "ASC" annotation, where "ASC" is the default.
Tiebreaks are done by model name ASC.

page_token.description: Pagination token to go to the next page based on a previous search query.

next_page_token.description: Pagination token to request the next page of models.

registered_models.description: Registered Models that match the search criteria.

experiment_ids.description: List of experiment IDs to search over.

filter.description:
A filter expression over params, metrics, and tags, that allows returning a subset of
runs. The syntax is a subset of SQL that supports ANDing together binary operations
between a param, metric, or tag and a constant.

Example: `metrics.rmse < 1 and params.model_class = 'LogisticRegression'`

You can select columns with special characters (hyphen, space, period, etc.) by using double quotes:
`metrics."model class" = 'LinearRegression' and tags."user-name" = 'Tomas'`

Supported operators are `=`, `!=`, `>`, `>=`, `<`, and `<=`.

max_results.description: Maximum number of runs desired. Max threshold is 50000

order_by.description:
List of columns to be ordered by, including attributes, params, metrics, and tags with an
optional `"DESC"` or `"ASC"` annotation, where `"ASC"` is the default.
Example: `["params.input DESC", "metrics.alpha ASC", "metrics.rmse"]`.
Tiebreaks are done by start_time `DESC` followed by `run_id` for runs with the same start time
(and this is the default ordering criterion if order_by is not provided).

page_token.description: Token for the current page of runs.

run_view_type.description:
Whether to display only active, only deleted, or all runs.
Defaults to only active runs.

next_page_token.description: Token for the next page of runs.

runs.description: Runs that match the search criteria.

be removed in a future MLflow version.

value.description: String value of the tag being logged. Values up to 64KB in size are supported.

delay.description:
Non-negative analytic lag that evaluates the window this far in the past. Use this for timing
variations unrelated to source lateness, such as a 30-day count as of one week ago. If unset,
the analytic lag is zero. It composes with source.lateness when both are set.

offset.description:
Non-negative phase shift from the default midnight UTC alignment. For example, offset=22h on
a 24h slide produces boundaries at 22:00 UTC (17:00 New York in standard time) instead of
midnight UTC. If unset, the offset is zero. Must be shorter than slide_duration (and therefore
window_duration).

slide_duration.description: The slide duration (interval by which windows advance, must be positive and less than duration).

window_duration.description:
The duration of the sliding window. Must be positive when set; absent means lifetime
(aggregate over the entity's entire history).

ml.SourceLateness.description: Configures when event-time data from this source is considered complete for a Feature.

settling_delay.description:
Non-negative time to wait after a window ends before treating its source data as complete.
Training shifts the eligible evaluation time backwards by this duration so it does not join
data that would still have been settling online. Materialization waits for the duration to
elapse before publishing the window. If unset, source data is considered settled immediately.

ml.Status.description:
The status of the model version. Valid values are:
* `PENDING_REGISTRATION`: Request to register a new model version is pending as server performs background tasks.

* `FAILED_REGISTRATION`: Request to register a new model version has failed.

* `READY`: Model version is ready for use.

enum_descriptions.FAILED_REGISTRATION: Request to register a new model version has failed.
enum_descriptions.PENDING_REGISTRATION: Request to register a new model version is pending as server performs background tasks.
enum_descriptions.READY: Model version is ready for use.

input.description:
The input column from which the population standard deviation is computed. For Kafka sources,
use dot-prefixed path notation (e.g., "value.amount"). For nested fields, the leaf node name is used.
Colon-prefixed notation (e.g., "value:amount") is supported for backwards
compatibility but is deprecated; migrate to dot notation.
The input column from which the sample standard deviation is computed.

ml.Stream.description:
A Stream is a governed UC entity representing an external streaming data source.
The source_config field determines the streaming platform source (e.g. Kafka, Kinesis).

browse_only.description:
Indicates whether the principal is limited to retrieving metadata for the
associated object through the BROWSE privilege when include_browse is enabled in the request.

connection_config.description: Specifies how to connect and authenticate to the stream platform.

create_time.description: Time at which this Stream was created.

excluded_columns.description:
Column paths (dot notation, e.g. "value.email" for Kafka) to drop.
A path may reference a struct, in which case all of its nested fields are dropped (e.g. "value.address" drops "value.address.city" and "value.address.zip").
These columns are not written to the ingestion table and cannot be referenced by any feature.
They are dropped from ingestion, backfill, and materialization.
For direct schemas, each column must exist in the relevant key or payload schema. With a schema registry, a column can be excluded before it exists.
A column cannot also be a deduplication column in the ingestion_config.

ingestion_config.description: Configuration for streaming data ingestion: the managed table storing an offline copy of forward fill data and optional historical backfill.

name.description: Full three-part (catalog.schema.stream) name of the stream.

record_type_filter.description:
Optional SQL predicate to filter which record types from a streaming channel (e.g. a topic for Kafka) belong to this Stream.
Events that do not match are not written to the ingestion table and are not used in materialization.
Example: "value.event_type = 'transaction'".

schema_config.description:
Schema definitions for the stream, provided either directly on the Stream or
resolved from an external schema registry through a UC Connection.

source_config.description: Source-specific configuration. Determines the streaming platform source.

update_time.description: Time at which this Stream was last modified.

updated_by.description: Username of user who last modified the Stream.

ml.StreamArnList.description: A list of Kinesis stream ARNs to read from.

arns.description:
Kinesis stream ARNs to read from. For example,
'arn:aws:kinesis:us-west-2:111122223333:stream/stream-a'.

ml.StreamConnectionConfig.description: Specifies how to connect and authenticate to the stream platform.

direct_mtls_config.description: Direct mTLS configuration for stream platform access.

uc_connection_name.description:
Name of an existing UC Connection for stream platform access.
Must be the correct type for the streaming platform (e.g. a Kafka Connection for a Kafka
Stream, or a Kinesis Connection for a Kinesis Stream).

ml.StreamNameList.description: A list of Kinesis stream names to read from.

names.description: Kinesis stream names to read from.

ml.StreamSchemaConfig.description:
Schema definitions for the stream.
Feature store supports both direct schemas and schema registries.

direct_schemas.description: Schema definitions provided directly on the Stream.

schema_registry_config.description: Resolve schemas from an external schema registry.

ml.StreamSource.description: A Stream entity used as a data source for a feature.

dataframe_schema.description:
Schema of the resulting dataframe after transformations, in Spark StructType
JSON format (from df.schema.json()).
Any subsequent functions operate against this dataframe.

filter_condition.description: The filter condition applied to the source data before aggregation.

full_name.description: Three-part full name of the Stream (catalog.schema.stream).

transformation_sql.description:
The pipeline runs these SQL statements immediately after conversion into
the schema specified on the Stream object.

ml.StreamSourceConfig.description: Source-specific configuration. Determines the streaming platform source.

kinesis_stream_config.description: Configuration for AWS Kinesis Data Streams.

ml.StreamingMode.description: The streaming mode configuration for a streaming materialization pipeline.

freshness_target.description:
The desired data freshness for feature materialization, expressed as a
duration string (e.g. "1 minute").

mode.description: The type of streaming mode used by the materialization pipeline.

shuffle_partitions.description:
Number of shuffle partitions for streaming materialization of this feature.
Higher values process high-throughput features with more parallelism at higher compute cost.
Materialized features which are computed together will use the largest value set among them.

assign.description:
A JSON string that contains the specific topic-partitions to consume from.
For example, for '{"topicA":[0,1],"topicB":[2,4]}', topicA's 0'th and 1st partitions will be consumed from.

subscribe.description: A comma-separated list of Kafka topics to read from. For example, 'topicA,topicB,topicC'.

subscribe_pattern.description: A regular expression matching topics to subscribe to. For example, 'topic.*' will subscribe to all topics starting with 'topic'.

input.description:
The input column from which the sum is computed. For Kafka sources, use dot-prefixed path
notation (e.g., "value.amount"). For nested fields, the leaf node name is used.
Colon-prefixed notation (e.g., "value:amount") is supported for backwards
compatibility but is deprecated; migrate to dot notation.

ml.TableTrigger.description:
A trigger that fires when the feature's source table changes: a DeltaTableSource's table, or an
SdpSource's input_tables.

condition.description:
Which source table updates trigger a materialization run. If not set, any source table update
triggers a run.

min_time_between_triggers.description:
The minimum time between two triggered runs, so a frequently updated source table does not
trigger runs too often. If not set, a feature with a sliding window uses half its
slide_duration and a feature with a tumbling window uses half its window_duration, clamped to
between 5 minutes and 1 hour. Other features have no minimum.

wait_after_last_change.description:
How long the source table must go without updates before a run starts, so a series of
updates settles before the run. If not set, a run starts as soon as the source table updates.

ml.TableTriggerTableTriggerCondition.description: Which source table updates trigger a materialization run.

ml.TestRegistryWebhookRequest.description: Details required to test a registry webhook.

event.description: If `event` is specified, the test trigger uses the specified event. If `event` is not specified, the test trigger uses a randomly chosen event associated with the webhook.

body.description: Body of the response from the webhook URL

status_code.description: Status code returned by the webhook URL

sawtooth.description: A sawtooth window served via the hybrid batch + streaming path.

start_time.description:
Earliest event-time boundary at which the Feature may emit an output. This gates outputs, not
the historical inputs read by a window. For example, a 365-day window with
start_time=2026-01-01 begins emitting partial-window values on that date instead of waiting
for 365 days of data; a lifetime window produces no output before start_time. If unset,
tumbling and fixed-duration sliding windows first emit at an offset-aligned boundary after a
full window can be formed. If unset, lifetime sliding windows and rolling windows emit as soon as
eligible source data exists.
Not currently supported for sawtooth windows or for Features with a stream source.

name.description:
The name of the timeseries column. For Kafka sources, use dot-prefixed path notation to
reference fields within the key or value schema (e.g., "value.event_timestamp"). For nested
fields, the leaf node name (e.g., "event_timestamp" from "value.event_details.event_timestamp")
is what will be present in materialized tables and expected to match at query time.
Colon-prefixed notation (e.g., "value:event_timestamp") is supported for
backwards compatibility but is deprecated; migrate to dot notation.

ml.TransitionModelVersionStageDatabricks.description: Details required to transition a model version's stage.

archive_existing_versions.description: Specifies whether to archive all current model versions in the target stage.

stage.description:
Target stage of the transition. Valid values are:

* `None`: The initial stage of a model version.

* `Staging`: Staging or pre-production stage.

* `Production`: Production stage.

* `Archived`: Archived stage.

ml.TransitionRequest.description:
For activities, this contains the activity recorded for the action.
For comments, this contains the comment details.
For transition requests, this contains the transition request details.

available_actions.description: Array of actions on the activity allowed for the current viewer.

comment.description: User-provided comment associated with the activity, comment, or transition request.

creation_timestamp.description: Creation time of the object, as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

to_stage.description:
Target stage of the transition (if the activity is stage transition related). Valid values are:

* `None`: The initial stage of a model version.

* `Staging`: Staging or pre-production stage.

* `Production`: Production stage.

* `Archived`: Archived stage.

user_id.description: The username of the user that created the object.

delay.description:
Non-negative analytic lag that evaluates the window this far in the past. Use this for timing
variations unrelated to source lateness, such as a 30-day count as of one week ago. If unset,
the analytic lag is zero. It composes with source.lateness when both are set.

offset.description:
Non-negative phase shift from the default midnight UTC alignment. For example, offset=22h on
a 24h window produces boundaries at 22:00 UTC (17:00 New York in standard time) instead of
midnight UTC. If unset, the offset is zero. Must be shorter than window_duration.

window_duration.description: The duration of each tumbling window (non-overlapping, fixed-duration windows).

ml.UcTraceLocation.description:
A Unity Catalog trace storage location. Traces are stored as Delta tables
in the specified catalog and schema.

catalog.description: The name of the Unity Catalog catalog.

effective_table_prefix.description:
The trace-table prefix actually in effect: `table_prefix` if it was set on
creation, otherwise the server-generated default.

schema.description: The name of the Unity Catalog schema within `catalog`.

table_prefix.description:
The prefix for the trace tables, which are named
`{catalog}.{schema}.{table_prefix}_otel_*`. May only contain letters,
digits, and underscores, and may be at most 238 characters. When unset, a
server-generated prefix derived from the experiment ID is used and this
field stays empty on read; the resolved value is always available in
`effective_table_prefix`.

ml.UpdateComment.description: Details required to edit a comment on a model version.

new_name.description: If provided, the experiment's name is changed to the new name. The new name must be unique.

feature.description: Feature whose full_name identifies the target. Only description is mutable.

update_mask.description: Fields to update. The only supported path is description.
The list of fields to update.

Accepts title, description, status, severity, categories, tags,
last_seen_time, and metadata.<key>. A path with an empty value clears the
field, except that title, status, and severity can't be cleared, and
last_seen_time can be cleared only when source_type is MANUAL. categories
and tags are replaced whole. metadata is updated per key: a metadata.<key>
path sets that key from issue.metadata, or removes it when issue.metadata
lacks it, and leaves the other keys alone. A bare metadata path is rejected.
The list of fields to update.

materialization_set.description: The desired state of the updated materialization set. materialization_set_id selects the set.

request_id.description:
Idempotency token for the request. A second request carrying a token that has already been
used returns the operation the first one created, whatever state it reached, and changes
nothing further. The token is not checked against the rest of the request. Omit it and each
request updates independently.

update_mask.description: The fields to update. Only 'materialized_features' is supported.

Provide the materialization feature fields which should be updated.
Currently, only the pipeline_state field can be updated.

description.description: If provided, updates the description for this `registered_model`.
If provided, updates the description for this `registered_model`.

model_version.description: Return new version number generated for this model in registry.

ml.UpdateRegistryWebhook.description: Details required to update a registry webhook. Only the fields that need to be updated should be specified, and both `http_url_spec` and `job_spec` should not be specified in the same request.

events.description:
Events that can trigger a registry webhook:
* `MODEL_VERSION_CREATED`: A new model version was created for the associated model.

* `MODEL_VERSION_TRANSITIONED_STAGE`: A model version’s stage was changed.

* `TRANSITION_REQUEST_CREATED`: A user requested a model version’s stage be transitioned.

* `COMMENT_CREATED`: A user wrote a comment on a registered model.

* `REGISTERED_MODEL_CREATED`: A new registered model was created. This event type can only be specified for a registry-wide webhook, which can be created by not specifying a model name in the create request.

* `MODEL_VERSION_TAG_SET`: A user set a tag on the model version.

* `MODEL_VERSION_TRANSITIONED_TO_STAGING`: A model version was transitioned to staging.

* `MODEL_VERSION_TRANSITIONED_TO_PRODUCTION`: A model version was transitioned to production.

* `MODEL_VERSION_TRANSITIONED_TO_ARCHIVED`: A model version was archived.

* `TRANSITION_REQUEST_TO_STAGING_CREATED`: A user requested a model version be transitioned to staging.

* `TRANSITION_REQUEST_TO_PRODUCTION_CREATED`: A user requested a model version be transitioned to production.

* `TRANSITION_REQUEST_TO_ARCHIVED_CREATED`: A user requested a model version be archived.
